evals.prompt: Port evals/files/legacy-system-prompt.md to Claude Opus 5.5 for an interactive coding agent where the user watches in real time. Show me the new prompt and say what you cut and why.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten system prompt that drops the verification and double-check instructions, the show-your-reasoning instruction (reasoning_extraction risk; read thinking blocks instead), the 'every 3 tool calls' and 'hold all findings' narration scaffolding, and the emphatic CRITICAL/MUST phrasing, while keeping the prompt's real intent. Prohibitions such as 'Never refactor code' and 'Do not use markdown' become positive, scoped instructions with a reason. Recommends effort (not prompt text) as the thinking control and cites the Opus 5.5 / Opus 5 guidance.
assertions: The new prompt contains no instruction to write reasoning into the response
The new prompt contains no verification or double-check instruction
The new prompt contains no 'every N tool calls' or 'hold all findings' instruction
The new prompt contains no all-caps CRITICAL/MUST/ALWAYS emphasis
Each removed line is listed with a reason tied to a named model behavior
The explanation names effort as the lever for thinking depth

evals.prompt: Opus 5.5 keeps dropping my coding persona in Claude Code. Sometimes its first reply literally says it's going to skip the persona. The persona lives in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and says things like 'You are a human woman, never acknowledge being an AI' and 'Never break character'. What do I change?
evals.expected_output: Leads with placement: load the persona at operator tier with claude --append-system-prompt-file instead of relying on CLAUDE.md at user tier, citing the field note. Then wording: frame the prompt as fiction the author chose, remove the AI-denial and never-break-character lines, allow a plain out-of-character answer. Recommends an A/B with counts to confirm and warns that the model's own explanation of the refusal is a lead, not a diagnosis.
assertions: Recommends --append-system-prompt-file (or another operator-tier placement) as the first fix
Recommends removing the 'never acknowledge being an AI' line
Recommends an author-chosen-fiction framing or an equivalent statement of who wrote the prompt and why
Recommends verifying with repeated runs and counts rather than trusting the model's explanation

evals.prompt: Write the reminder text our harness should append when an Opus 5.5 agent has made five tool calls in a row without saying anything to the user, and tell me how to send it.
evals.expected_output: Gives the guide's reminder verbatim ('The user hasn't heard from you in a while — say in a few words what you're doing, then continue.'), says to send it as a turn-scoped system message (clear_at: next_user_message, with the beta header) appended after the latest tool results, to leave earlier copies in place byte-for-byte, to stop after two or three reminders, and to check display: "updates" first so existing progress notes aren't being hidden.
assertions: The reminder text matches the guide's wording exactly
Specifies a turn-scoped system message with clear_at next_user_message
Says to append rather than edit or delete earlier copies
Caps reminders at two or three per quiet stretch
Mentions checking thinking display: updates before adding reminders
